title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 12th District
area: Most of Mercer County (Trenton, Princeton) plus parts of Middlesex and Somerset counties, including Plainfield and parts of Piscataway.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman (D) did not seek re-election and withdrew from the Democratic primary ballot, leaving NJ-12 an open seat for the first time since 2014. Adam Hamawy won a 13-candidate Democratic primary on June 2, 2026 with 28.6% of the vote. Gregg Mele won the Republican primary unopposed. Andres Jinete (Green Party) and Winston Jordan (No Party Affiliation) also qualified for the November 3 general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Adam Hamawy
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 28.6% of the vote in a 13-candidate field

summary.text: Adam Hamawy is the Democratic nominee for New Jersey's open 12th Congressional District. A plastic and reconstructive surgeon and U.S. Army veteran who reached the rank of lieutenant colonel, he served as a combat trauma surgeon in Iraq and has volunteered as a physician in conflict and disaster zones, including Gaza in 2024 and 2025. He won a 13-candidate Democratic primary on June 2, 2026, and has not previously held elected office. He is running on Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and economic policies aimed at working families.

background.text: According to his campaign website, his family came to New Jersey when he was seven months old, and he grew up in Plainfield and Old Bridge and attended public schools.

Enlisted in the New Jersey Army National Guard in 1989 and served until 1991; graduated from Rutgers University, New Brunswick, in 1991 with a biology major, using an ROTC scholarship. He later graduated from New Jersey Medical School (now part of Rutgers University-Newark) in 1996, and Ballotpedia also lists a graduate degree from Rutgers University at Camden.

Made his first volunteer humanitarian medical mission in 1994 as a medical student, working with the United Nations to deliver medical supplies to hospitals in Bosnia, according to his campaign website.
On September 11, 2001, while a surgical resident in New York, he treated victims and first responders at a field hospital at Ground Zero.

Served in the U.S. Army from 2003 to 2011, rising to lieutenant colonel, including as a combat trauma surgeon in Iraq; WHYY reports he is credited with helping save the life of Sen. Tammy Duckworth in Iraq.
After his service, worked in New Jersey emergency rooms and built his own medical practice in Princeton; WHYY describes him as a plastic and reconstructive surgeon with an office in Princeton.

Has volunteered as a physician in war and disaster zones for about 30 years, including Haiti, Sudan, Syria, Lebanon and Turkey; during 2024 and 2025 medical missions to Gaza he was among a group that was unable to leave when the Rafah Crossing was seized.
Was Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman's guest at the 2025 State of the Union address. Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary to succeed the retiring Watson Coleman.
Per WHYY, he lives in South Brunswick with his wife and has four children.

priorities.text: Achieving universal healthcare through Medicare for All rather than continued military spending, saying "we have our priorities wrong as a country."
priorities.quote: Healthcare, Not Bombs - We have our priorities wrong as a country. We should be spending our resources on achieving universal healthcare through Medicare for All, not bombs and endless wars.

priorities.text: Abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), saying immigrant communities are under attack from federal agencies he describes as "out of control."
priorities.quote: Abolish ICE - Our immigrant neighbors are under attack and federal agencies like ICE are out of control. We need to protect our neighbors and restore civil rights in this country.

priorities.text: "Unrigging" the economy so it works for working people rather than what he calls "billionaires at the top."

positions.summary: Supports achieving universal healthcare through Medicare for All.
positions.quote: We should be spending our resources on achieving universal healthcare through Medicare for All, not bombs and endless wars.

positions.summary: Supports abolishing ICE, saying the agency is "out of control" and that immigrant communities need protection.

candidates.name: Gregg Mele
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Gregg Mele is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's open 12th Congressional District. An attorney who has worked in business and finance and taught graduate courses, he has run for office repeatedly since 2018 as an independent, a Libertarian and a Republican; WHYY reports he has run unsuccessfully seven times. He ran unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary, and his campaign website lists lower costs, border security and public safety, accountable government, and support for Israel among his priorities.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was raised by blue-collar parents; WHYY reports he is a lifelong New Jersey resident.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Montclair State University and a law degree; Ballotpedia also lists graduate degrees from Stevens Institute of Technology, New York University and CUNY Baruch College.

His campaign website says he built a career in law, business, finance, technology and the classroom. WHYY reports he practices law (corporate law, contracts, securities, real estate and estate planning), previously worked on Wall Street, and has taught graduate-level courses, including at Stevens Institute of Technology.

Ran for the U.S. House in New Jersey's 7th District in 2018 on the Freedom, Responsibility, Action Party line, receiving 0.8% of the vote, and in 2019 was the Libertarian candidate for mayor of Bridgewater.
Was the Libertarian nominee for governor in 2021, finishing fourth with 0.3% of the vote.

Running as a Republican, did not make the 2022 primary ballot for the 6th District; in 2024 he first sought the Republican U.S. Senate nomination, then ran in the 6th District Republican primary, losing to Scott Fegler 81.6% to 18.4%.
Won the 2026 Republican primary in the 12th District unopposed, 13,298 votes.
Lives in Plainfield with his wife and has two children, according to WHYY.

priorities.text: Lowering family costs through disciplined federal spending, expanded American energy production, and relief from regulation.
Securing the border and supporting law enforcement to keep communities safe.
Requiring Congress to answer what new spending will cost, how it will be paid for, and whether it will work before approving it.
priorities.quote: Make Congress answer three questions before spending: What will it cost? How will it be paid for? Will it actually work?

positions.summary: Supports securing the border and enforcing immigration law.
Supports law enforcement funding as part of keeping New Jersey communities safe.
Supports standing with Israel and strengthening American leadership abroad.
Says he will "put patients first" by expanding choice and protecting the doctor-patient relationship from what he calls "one-size-fits-all Washington control," rather than expanding public coverage.
Campaign platform calls for defending parental rights and keeping schools focused on academic excellence, framed as part of protecting parents' role in education decisions.

summary.text: Andres Jinete is the Green Party nominee for New Jersey's open 12th Congressional District. A community organizer from Bound Brook and a member of the Central Jersey Tenant Union, he has worked in libraries in the district and on rapid-response networks opposing ICE detentions. He has not held elected office and is running on rent control, universal health care and abolishing ICE.

background.text: Born and raised in Bound Brook, New Jersey, where he lives; WHYY reports he was 29 at the time of its September 2026 voter guide.
Is a management student at Kean University, according to WHYY.
Worked at libraries in the 12th District for about 10 years (WHYY) and at the community library setting up programs for adults, seniors and families, according to his campaign website.

Is a member of the Central Jersey Tenant Union, representing one of the largest apartment complexes in Bound Brook, and says his advocacy for tenants and seniors led to code violations being addressed.

Helped build rapid-response networks across New Jersey to support working people and small businesses and to prevent ICE detentions; also a member of Workers Strike Back and a steering committee member of the Latinx caucus of the Green Party.

priorities.text: National rent control covering residential and commercial properties, plus large-scale investment in income-based social housing.
priorities.quote: We are fighting for national rent control that includes residential and commercial properties, and for a massive investment in social housing which will provide high-quality, income based units.

priorities.text: Universal, single-payer healthcare and a patent-free drug market.
priorities.quote: The insurance companies and Big Pharma use both the Democrat and Republican parties to hold back single-payer healthcare and a patent-free drug market.

priorities.text: Purchasing and forgiving all outstanding federal student loan debt and reinstating tuition-free public colleges and universities.

positions.summary: Supports national rent control for residential and commercial properties and a major expansion of income-based social housing.
Supports single-payer, universal healthcare and a patent-free drug market.
Has organized rapid-response networks in New Jersey aimed at preventing ICE detentions in communities.

summary.text: Winston Jordan is a candidate for New Jersey's open 12th Congressional District who describes himself as a progressive running a "no money, no donation" campaign. An Army veteran, he worked as a computer systems analyst, engineer and IT executive. He has not previously held elected office and is running on a "Get Money Out" platform, according to WHYY.

background.text: Born in Brooklyn, New York; WHYY reports he is 68 and lives in Hopewell Township, New Jersey.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1976 to 1978 and earned a military citation from Big Bend Community College in 1977.
Worked as a computer systems analyst, engineer and IT executive, according to WHYY; Ballotpedia also lists author among his career experience.

priorities.text: Running a campaign that accepts no donations from individuals, corporations, PACs, unions, or lobbies of any kind.
priorities.quote: I accept absolutely no campaign money of any kind — not small-dollar, not large-dollar, not from individuals, not from corporations, PACs, unions, lobbies, or any entity whatsoever.

priorities.text: Redirecting federal resources directly to residents of NJ-12 rather than corporate beneficiaries of federal policy, including free education and direct investment to eliminate poverty.
Reviving New Deal-era economic guarantees, describing his platform as "FDR2.0" and citing the rights to a useful job, a living wage, adequate medical care, and a decent home.

positions.summary: Cites "the right to adequate medical care and the opportunity to achieve and enjoy good health" among the New Deal-era guarantees he wants restored.

researchNotes: Adam Hamawy's and Andres Jinete's positions and priorities are drawn from their Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers (their own words); Winston Jordan's from a 2025 survey he completed. Gregg Mele has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, so his positions are drawn from his campaign website's issue summaries rather than direct Q&A, and his campaign website has no dedicated biography page, so his background draws on Ballotpedia, his homepage, WHYY and the New Jersey Globe. No candidate in this race has held prior elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record to report for any of them. Biographies for Gregg Mele, Andres Jinete and Winston Jordan are brief because little public record exists beyond Ballotpedia, campaign pages and local news; sources differ on which law school awarded Mele's law degree, so it is not named.
